text.en: In verse 1, Sharp's printed words and his treble part have "O sisters too", but his tenor and bass parts spell it "two": the mother may be speaking to the two other women on stage with her.
text.es: En la estrofa 1, la letra impresa de Sharp y su voz superior dicen "O sisters too" (oh, hermanas, también), pero sus voces de tenor y de bajo escriben "two" (dos): la madre quizá habla a las otras dos mujeres que están en escena con ella.

source.en: Thomas Sharp, A Dissertation on the Pageants or Dramatic Mysteries Anciently Performed at Coventry (Coventry: Merridew and Son, 1825), p. 113 and the plates numbered 116 and 117; copy digitized by Google, holding library not named, read from the scan

text.en: In the 1591 setting, every "lullay" that ends the refrain, verse 1 or verse 3 closes on a major chord in this minor-key song, the treble on B natural, not B-flat. Verse 2 alone ends on a bare open chord, with no third.
text.es: En el arreglo de 1591, cada "lullay" que cierra el estribillo, la estrofa 1 o la estrofa 3 termina en un acorde mayor, en una canción en tono menor: la voz superior canta Si becuadro, no Si bemol. Solo la estrofa 2 termina en un acorde abierto, sin tercera.

source.en: Thomas Sharp, A Dissertation on the Pageants or Dramatic Mysteries Anciently Performed at Coventry (Coventry: Merridew and Son, 1825), "Song II" on the plates numbered 116 and 117 (treble, tenor and bass); copy digitized by Google, holding library not named, read from the scan
